reason: T2=T4 identical; T2/T4/T3 render Su 其心見於外而物安之 as "not revealed" (source has no 不) and T2 garbles 而妄之不猶存; T1 turns Huang 無所不為 into "doing nothing" (inverting the key claim); T3 also reads 經 as "the classics" and drops 取天下常以無為 from Lü, recasting the conclusion

T2 recovers the OCR-garbled 刖者之屨 (shoes of the footless, as Legge) and renders 取妻者止於外不得復使 as the husband freed from service, but appends 而況全德之人乎 which is past the page; T1 reads 胎者之屢 as a fetus and makes the wives stopped at the gates; T3 makes the opening "one feeds a child", collapses the shoes clause into a vague "failure to act" sentence, and also makes the wife the one kept outside

T1 and T2 render the dialogue and the eleven marginal glosses alike (inheriting the OCR 飲 for 斂); T3 reads the gloss 字法○ (character-technique mark) as "the word stopped/method", adds a note that 飲無崖 means immersion in the Tao, and makes 避影 "avoiding his own reflection" rather than Laozi's shadow

All three render the retreat to the marsh, the birds/beasts and the five calamities of 吾再逐於魯…圍於陳蔡 as Legge; all mishandle the fragment 責焉 (T2 "Regarding this responsibility", T3 "blamed him"); T1 additionally splits 辭其交遊 into Confucius saying "You have declined it" before the narrative "gave up social associations"

T2 follows the source/Legge through 知丘之適楚也以丘為必使楚王之召己 and 羞聞其言, slipping only on the gloss 摯妻 ("Zhi took his wife", 摯 read as a name); T1 merges the Chu journey and the summons into one cause, softens 羞聞其言 to "the very thought", and renders 滅裂 "overly simplistic"; T3 reads 著於己 as "famous for my ambitions" against Legge's "understand him well"

Source 如而夫者 = 'an ordinary man' (Legge 'one of those ordinary men'): T2 renders it, T1 and T3 read it as 'if one acts like him' and invent a duplicate humble-walking passage; T3 also reads 呂鉅 (haughty stride) as a person 'Lü Ju', losing the first of the three arrogant steps, and garbles 孰協唐許 as 'Agreement or harm?'; T1 drops the Xu You comparison from the main text; T2 keeps all three steps and Xu You but misparses 孰協唐許 as 'Tang and Xu said' and fuses glosses into the main text

Source 以狀而見親 = treated as kin BECAUSE OF FORM: T1 says 'because of their nature' (inverted) but keeps the full lists 熊羆狼豹豼貅虎 and 雕鶡鷹鳶; T2 keeps the form/kinship logic but drops 狼/羆 and one of the four raptors; T3 is the reference verbatim including the preceding-page passage on similarity of form and the seven-foot man, and the next-page closing sentence, which are not on this page; T4 inverts 未必無人心…見疏 into 'one with a human heart and human appearance is regarded with alienation' and collapses the same lists

俾也可忘 (Legge 'would he then allow me to be forgotten?'): T1 inverts it to 'How can I ever forget him?'; 報我不述 ('respond to me contrary to all reason'): T3 'repays me without following the proper way' is right, T1 'does not report back to me' and T2 'you do not mention a response' misread it; T1 also turns the three fanqie glosses (冒从目 / 呼到反 / 報反) into one spelling of 冒

Three-year mourning list 君與父母妻後子 (Legge/Mei 'ruler, parents, wife, and the first-born son'): T1 and T2 drop 後子, T3 keeps it; Motse's closing 國之治…治之廢則國之治亦廢 ('orderly because governed; when government is abandoned order disappears') is rendered by T3, while T1 and T2 make it a tautology ('if governance is abandoned, governance is abandoned'); all three garble the opening 不能為禍福執無祥不祥 similarly

安(能)誅之, which the page's own note glosses 安猶則 ('then'; Dubs 'then if he should seek out and kill'): T1 'then that lord must punish them' and T2 'how then can one not punish it' keep the affirmation, T3 'how could he punish them?' turns it into doubt; T3 also makes the heir 'the ancestors of the imperial lineage' (天下之宗室); otherwise all three follow the root text and the six notes

T3 alone renders 非約隨眠以留惑故 correctly ('not latent tendencies, as the bodhisattva retains delusions'); T1/T2/T4 collapse it into 'not regarding keeping/remaining seeds'; T1 renders 上心 as 'coarse mind', T2=T4 identical, split 四住人執 and read 生起 as 'birth and death'; all carry the three defiled minds and commentary

All carry §6 end, §7, §8 and the §9 heading as in source and Gemmell; T2 turns 如來有所說法耶 into 'any fixed teaching' (importing 定 from the answer) and drops 法 in 諸佛阿耨多羅三藐三菩提法; T1 and T3 = source throughout

All render the Sakridagamin and Anagamin passages as in source and Gemmell ('no going and coming', 'no not-coming'); T2 turns the truncated 色聲香味觸法是名須陀洹 into 'forms, sounds... are called stream-enterers', equating the sense objects with the stream-enterer; T1 and T3 keep it as the fragment it is

T3 keeps the root 依於智故生其苦樂覺心起念相應不斷 with 相應 ('associated and uninterrupted') and the commentary's 明起所依; T1 renders 智 as 'consciousness' and drops 相應; T2 drops 相應 and 明起所依; all carry the self/other continuity and the start of 執取相

All carry the question, the eight-fold answer, reason 1 (= Suzuki/Richard) and Fazang's 三苦二死 / 無上菩提大涅槃 gloss; T3 alone reads 總通兼正 as 'primary and secondary' and treats 非求世間名利等者 as a lemma ('Regarding not seeking...'); T1 and T2 turn the lemma into an assertion, T1 loosens 兼正 and glosses the two deaths wrongly, T2 renders 兼正 as 'the upright and the specific'

Source 此章先行而後文先本而後末: T2 renders action first, culture after; T1 and T3 misread 後文 as "subsequent text/later sections"; T3 also fuses 見其致 with 致猶委也 into "reaching for virtue is like yielding oneself", where T1/T2 gloss 致 as relinquish/devote; T1 renders 賢賢易色 as "as we appreciate beauty" against its own gloss 易其好色之心

Root 其爭也君子: T1 renders it (cf. Legge "in his contention he is still the Chun-tsze"); T2 and T3 cut 君子 off the sentence and attach it to the 聲去 tone note; T2 drops 哀痛 and reads 滅 as "reasons for their destruction"; T3 adds "the Master says", has the loser retrieve "arrows" where 升取 introduces taking the cup to drink, and misreads 位耦卒射亦如之 as "the position for the pairs"

T1 alone reads the Mencius allusion 惠而不知為政 ("kind but did not know how to govern") and 我子弟 as "our children and brothers", and renders 久而敬之 as respect maintained (= Legge), though it drops 及其卒也; T2 and T3 misparse 惠而不知為政 as "did not know that when he began to govern", turn 子弟 into "disciples" and inflate 久而敬之 to "the more he respected them"; T2 also drops 義 from 使民義; T3 drops 一時 and reads 未盡者誠 as "unsaid regarding his integrity"

Source 離色離相分第二十 三身具足: T3 numbers the section 20; T1 and T2 fold 三 into the title ("Twenty-Third") while also keeping "three bodies"; T1 also reverses 故受之以離色離相分 into "this section follows the Chapter on Parting"; all three render §19 = Gemmell (merit not real, therefore "much") and the §20 opening question

All four render the six stanzas and 持地菩薩 speech (cf. Soothill/Kern). Only T4 keeps 無等等 ("peerless", = Soothill "with which nothing can compare"); T2 drops it within "unsurpassed, equal, and correct"; T1 and T3 are identical, drop 無等等 and gloss 普門 with the spurious term "pumena"
